flags: point_count_corrected: request stated '25 points' and 'phi from 0 to 345 in 25 steps', but a clean 15-degree sweep from 0 to 345 (phi = 0,15,...,345) yields 24 points, not 25. A true 25-point split of the same range would require a non-round 14.375-degree step. Generated the standard 24-point, 15-degree grid instead of inventing an odd step size.
chunked_into_3_files: Fortran reader limits input files to 10 kinematic points each, so the 24 points were split 10/10/4.
explanation: All 24 kinematic points (W=1.6 GeV, Q2=1.0 GeV^2, cos(theta*)=0, phi*=0..345 deg in 15-deg steps) passed preflight (threshold, pole-safety, Q2, beam accessibility, table coverage, phi range, vcut all PASS). cos(theta*)=0 is well away from the +/-1 integration poles, so no kinematic correction was needed there. The only correction applied was resolving the internal inconsistency between the requested point count (25) and the requested phi range/step (0 to 345, which naturally gives 24 points at 15-degree spacing); the round, standard 15-degree azimuthal grid was kept rather than forcing a non-round step to hit exactly 25 points. Inputs were generated byte-compatible with the validated EXCLURAD format and chunked into 3 files of at most 10 points each per the Fortran reader's limit.
